title: observability signal rupture: metric islanding and trace-bridge remediation
creator: Sofia Reyes
description:
Summary:
During a cross-tenant compaction window on 2026-02-28 customers observed missing timeseries in LivePanels and gaps in span stitching for traces. Symptoms manifested as 'empty' dashboard tiles for high-cardinality metrics and partial traces where child spans could not be correlated to parents. Multiple paid customers escalated; incident produced elevated support pages and an interim mitigation.

Observed behaviour and impact:
- Metric islanding: certain tenant metric shards were diverted to a transient ingestion bucket during compaction. Those shard ranges were not rehydrated into the main metrics index for ~18 hours, resulting in missing timeseries in the Console and SLO alerts firing incorrectly.
- Trace-bridge failure: span indexing rotated mid-flight for short-lived requests. The span index compaction logic created non-monotonic sequence gaps; the trace-stitcher could not reconcile parent->child span references that crossed the rotation boundary.
- Affected environments: hosted (primary), Dedicated tenants on older agent versions, and Private VPCs without the recent checkpoint sync.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed in initial triage):
1) Shard compaction routine in telemetry-aggregator created a small window where writes for specific metric key ranges were routed to a temporary bucket to avoid write amplification. After compaction there was an edge-case where reattach of those ranges failed when sequence anchors were out-of-sync.
2) Trace index rotation used a best-effort checkpoint. Under sustained burst the checkpoint update lagged, producing non-monotonic sequence numbers for spans from short-lived worker processes. The trace-stitcher assumed monotonicity and dropped or mis-linked spans.

Proposed fix (phases):
Phase 1 (hotfix - immediate):
- Patch telemetry-aggregator to dual-write compaction-range writes to both temp and main index until reattach confirmation. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892)
- Add an emergency backfill job that replays the temp bucket into the main metrics index for the 2026-02-28 window. Backfill run scheduled and currently 70% complete.

Phase 2 (short-term durable):
- Make the compaction reattach atomic by publishing a 'range-ready' marker and using Redis-based distributed barrier to avoid races between reattach and routing logic.
- Add monotonic sequence enforcement to the span writer and a deterministic tombstone that trace-stitcher can use to bridge rotation boundaries.

Phase 3 (long-term resilience):
- Introduce per-tenant compaction quiesce windows and stronger telemetry alerting (see acceptance criteria) so compaction doesn't coincide with peak bursts for affected tenants.
- Add a console-level 'stale-tile' indicator and automated reconciliation job when tiles show >5 minutes of silence for non-zero expected traffic.

Acceptance criteria:
- Backfill job has rehydrated missing metric ranges and dashboards display historical data for affected ranges.
- Trace-stitcher reconciles previously orphaned child spans for the 2026-02-28 incident window.
- No additional customer reports of LivePanel blank tiles for the same tenants after release to console-2026.03.2.
- New compaction dual-write reduces probability of islanding to negligible levels (measured by synthetic test harness).

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy hotfix to a canary subset of ingestion nodes (region-us-west-2) for 1 hour, verify no regression in latency or write amplification.
2) Expand hotfix to all ingestion nodes and start backfill.
3) Deploy monotonic sequence enforcement to trace writers behind feature flag; enable for 10% of traffic and evaluate trace stitching correctness for 48h.
4) Gradually enable for 100% if metrics stable.

Customer communications and mitigation:
- Support: templated customer email drafted and approved by CX (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/OBS-2026/metric-islanding-communication).
- SRE playbook updated with runbook steps for detecting and reattaching temp buckets (Drive doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/obs/runbooks/compaction-reattach).

Monitoring and dashboards to add:
- Compaction-reattach-fail metric and 5m alert.
- Temporary bucket depth and backfill progress tile in SRE LivePanel.
- Trace-stitcher dropped-span rate with tenant-level breakdown.
comments: 2026-03-01: Triage call with SRE/Telemetry/Console. Agreed hotfix path and backfill. - Sofia

2026-03-02: Hotfix PR opened and reviewed. Initial code changes to dual-write compaction ranges. Code review feedback from Priya (observability) applied. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892 - Jonah
2026-03-03: Canary deployed to us-west-2 ingestion nodes. 0.4% increase in tail-latency observed; reverted minor buffer flush config and redeployed. Canary stable after 30m. - Jonah
2026-03-04: Backfill job started (job id backfill-20260304-1). Progress 70% as of 2026-03-08. Early verification shows dashboards recovering historical lines. - SRE
2026-03-05: Customer comms approved; first set of impacted customers notified with ETA and mitigation steps. - CX
2026-03-07: Added unit + integration tests for monotonic sequence enforcement. Local simulations show trace-stitcher reconciling orphan spans. Preparing feature-flag rollout. - Eng QA
2026-03-08: Security review not required for the hotfix; longer-term changes will be evaluated. Planning postmortem draft and follow-ups. - Sofia
next_steps: Finish backfill (target 100% by 2026-03-10), roll out monotonic span writer behind flag to 10% traffic on 2026-03-11, monitor for dropped-span rate reduction, and schedule postmortem meeting 2026-03-13.
postmortem_plan: Draft RCA, timeline of events, contributing factors, compensating controls. Assign action owners for: compaction atomicity (ENG-912348), trace checkpoint resilience (ENG-912349), console stale-tile UX (DES-1342). Postmortem to be published to Confluence and linked from this ticket.
